Markets bounce back led by auto, bank stocks; Sensex surges nearly 1,000 pts, Nifty reclaims 25,500
 The 30-share BSE Sensex jumped 989.94 points, or 1.21%, to close at 83,021.75; During the day, it surged 1,012.06 points, or 1.23%, to 83,043.87
 Updated - November 19, 2026 06:24 pm IST - Mumbai 
 PTI READ LATER 
 SEE ALL 
 Remove 
 Representational image.
 | Photo Credit: Getty Images/iStockphoto
 Benchmark equity indices bounced back sharply on Thursday (November 19, 2026), with the Sensex climbing nearly 1,000 points and the Nifty settling above 25,500, led by a sharp rally in auto and bank stocks, sustained foreign fund inflows, and easing commodity prices.
 The 30-share BSE Sensex jumped 989.94 points, or 1.21%, to close at 83,021.75. During the day, it surged 1,012.06 points, or 1.23%, to 83,043.87.
 Stock markets fall in early trade dragged by IT firms, U.S. Fed sens The 50-share NSE Nifty climbed 286.35 points, or 1.14%, to end at 25,514.30.
 From the Sensex pack, Maruti Suzuki surged 7.58%, Mahindra & Mahindra 4.78%, Axis Bank 4.38%, Hindustan Unilever 4.22%, Bharat Electronics 2.12% and State Bank of India 2.11%.
 Infosys, Tata Consultancy Services, Tech Mahindra, HCL Technologies and InterGlobe Aviation were the laggards.
 "Indian equities extended their recovery despite weak Asian cues and concerns over a hawkish U.S. Fed, supported by sustained FII inflows and easing commodity prices, from copper to crude.
 “Record foreign inflows in November boosted market liquidity, while lower crude prices eased concerns over future inflation and external balances. Autos led the rally as falling copper and aluminium prices improved the margin outlook, while consumption and banking stocks also advanced, with banking indices reaching record highs," Vinod Nair, Head of Research, Geojit Investments Ltd., said.
 In Asian markets, South Korea's Kospi and Japan's Nikkei 225 ended higher, while Shanghai's SSE Composite index and Hong Kong's Hang Seng index settled lower.
 Markets in Europe were trading mostly higher.
 India’s Oct. crude import bill soars 87.5% to $19.5-bn amid West Asia tensions, volumes up 11% The U.S. equity markets ended mostly lower on Wednesday (November 18, 2026). The Dow Jones Industrial Average was down 1.11%, S&P 500 declined 0.23%, while Nasdaq Composite ended 0.42% higher.
 Brent crude, the global oil benchmark, was up 0.61% at $92.51 per barrel.
 Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) bought equities worth ₹5,866.78 crore on Wednesday (November 18, 2026), according to exchange data.
 In the previous session, the Sensex dropped 500.38 points, or 0.61%, to settle at 82,031.81. The Nifty declined 159.45 points, or 0.63%, to end at 25,227.95.
